title: AS3 adaptation priorities
description: Planning partitions of the complete declaration audit. Existing subset and partial evidence is retained; only missing behavior is an adaptation gap.
classificationPolicy: Library scopes are separated first. Explicit AS3 operators, statements and special types belong to the Player language foundation. For other declarations use detail_availability, then index availability; Flash means Player reference, AIR without Flash means AIR-documented, and no label stays unresolved. Owner defaults are compressed per-entry decisions, not class availability inherited by members. Exceptions preserve every differing member decision.

buckets.title: Flash Player reference
buckets.purpose: AS3 language, core and Player APIs; member and runtime-profile limits still apply.

buckets.title: Far future: AIR extensions
buckets.purpose: Declarations documented for AIR without Player availability. Far-future backlog, with no scheduled adaptation; revisit only after an explicit priority change.

buckets.title: Far future: libraries and platform extensions
buckets.purpose: Flash components, Flex/Spark, TLF and other supplied libraries. Far-future backlog, with no scheduled adaptation; executing on Player does not make them built-in APIs.

buckets.title: Platform not resolved
buckets.purpose: The reference does not establish Player or AIR availability; review before assigning an adaptation target.

groups.title: Important now: classic foundation
groups.purpose: Stages 1–6: mathematics, objects, MovieClip, display, drawing and text, in that order.

groups.title: Next: file audio and video
groups.purpose: Stage 7: ordinary audio/video playback after the classic foundation.

groups.title: Later: services and advanced Player APIs
groups.purpose: Stage 8: capture, networking, files, platform integration, storage, 3D, workers and specialized APIs.

groups.title: Far future: AIR extensions
groups.purpose: Declarations documented for AIR without Player availability. Far-future backlog, with no scheduled adaptation; revisit only after an explicit priority change.

groups.title: Far future: libraries and platform extensions
groups.purpose: Flash components, Flex/Spark, TLF and other supplied libraries. Far-future backlog, with no scheduled adaptation; executing on Player does not make them built-in APIs.

groups.title: Platform not resolved
groups.purpose: The reference does not establish Player or AIR availability; review before assigning an adaptation target.

stages.title: Mathematics and 2D geometry
stages.purpose: Numbers, mathematical operations, points, rectangles, matrices and color transforms.

stages.title: Objects, language and collections
stages.purpose: Object and class semantics, functions, collections, strings, errors, dates, regular expressions, XML and binary data.

stages.title: MovieClip and timeline
stages.purpose: MovieClip playback, frame labels, scenes and frame lifecycle events.

stages.title: Display, events and basic input
stages.purpose: Display trees, stage behavior, event dispatch, keyboard/mouse input and timers.

stages.title: Graphics, bitmaps and filters
stages.purpose: 2D drawing, bitmap pixels, image encoding and conventional visual filters.

stages.title: Text and fonts
stages.purpose: Classic text fields, text formatting, stylesheets, font access and text metrics.

stages.title: File audio and video playback
stages.purpose: Sound channels and transforms, video display and the file-playback part of NetStream.

stages.title: Services and advanced Player APIs
stages.purpose: Camera/microphone capture, network/files/platform/storage, loading, 3D, workers, Flash Text Engine and specialized profiles.

AS3:constructor:flash/desktop/Clipboard..note: The constructor is listed for Player but throws there; only generalClipboard is usable. This is a profile restriction, not a missing useful constructor.

limitations: Counts cover declarations of all kinds, not only functions, and are not a Flash compatibility percentage.
Player labels retain version, sandbox and profile limits; the list is not a promise of unrestricted HTML5 behavior.
AIR-documented without a Player label is a separate documentation bucket, not proof that every unlabeled historical runtime is incompatible.
Foundation priority is not an implementation status. implemented_subset and partial remain bounded; needs_review is neither implemented nor missing.
The audit is a dated evidence snapshot. This classification does not run tests or promote current source conformance.
A stage includes only its declared members: advanced members of shared classes may be deferred to stage 8.
